two_year_backfill_estimate.basis: COLLECTOR-PRICE-HISTORY-BACKFILL-20261111: 487 trading-day bundles per source (window 2024-11-10..2026-11-10); hosted collector serves 488 days each of TWSE, TPEx price history and T86. Rows per day are ESTIMATES (not measured: hosted state was not touched): TWSE ~1300, TPEx ~900, T86 ~1250. Per-pull limit is the definition cap max_records=500 (existing limit, not widened); schedule interval is the definition cadence 86400s
two_year_backfill_estimate.first_pull: First pull returns at most 500 rows per source, event-dated from the oldest bundle first. Bundle verification is windowed to the cap: per pull the adapter reads index.json, each touched bundle's manifest.json and items.jsonl (+status.json) and at most max_records(500) raw files (only the rows that can be returned are hash/size-verified; bundle_sha256 over declared hashes and items/manifest id coverage are verified for every touched bundle). Rows beyond the window are verified when the persisted resume cursor reaches them.
two_year_backfill_estimate.finding: At the definition cadence of one pull per day the cap drains only 500 rows per source per day, i.e. roughly 3-4 years per source: the two-year backfill is correct and resumable but not practical at steady cadence. Options (operator/Root decision, not done here because the task forbids widening limits and hosted/deploy changes): a temporary shorter interval for the three history connectors through the existing schedule command (hourly = ~53/37/51 days), or a one-off larger per-job cap; neither is changed by this task
two_year_backfill_estimate.official_truth: TW_OFFICIAL_HISTORY_MAX_MONTHS=2 untouched; official tw_price_daily records are never written by the collector path
